column3: description
planned
FALLBACK line size, used only if a unit row leaves line_cap blank.
Layer slots per unit.
Charge gained by departing with an empty line.
POWER = charge figured from the ability's base power. DEALT = from damage actually dealt.
Superseded by the matchups sheet; kept as a fallback.
Superseded by the matchups sheet; kept as a fallback.
Whether a blocked attack still rotates the layer queue.
Below this fraction of max MS the ceiling chevron pulses red.
Length of the death sequence.
Broken layers stay gone until the round ends, then regrow at the back of the queue.
How long each charge segment holds before the next.
How long a station takes to fly across and strike the target.
Delay between letters of dialogue.
How long a finished line stays on screen before it fades.
Fraction of max MS below which the winning / losing lines fire.
Every this-much overflow (as a fraction of max MS) forces one more corrupted slot.
Chance the AI takes a random affordable attack instead of its best one.
Chance the AI prefers an ability with charge segments when it can afford one.
Re-order every unit's layer queue at the start of each round.
Each charge segment in a line grants the OPPONENT one temporary slot next turn.
FALLBACK cap on temporary slots, used only if a unit row leaves max_bonus_slots blank.
Abilities shown per page in the Emotions panel.
Gap between one temporary slot flying in and the next.
How far a pointer must travel across the panel to count as a page swipe.
How much an accumulating tag grows once it holds a full max-MS worth of change.
Breathing period of an accumulating tag holding almost nothing.
Breathing period of a tag holding a full max-MS worth — it flashes far harder.
Gauge canvas width in logical pixels. Lower = chunkier pixels, coarser value steps.
Gauge canvas height in logical pixels — tall enough for the end caps.
Height of the bar's interior, before the wave, in logical pixels.
Wave amplitude on the bar's silhouette (reference: 9.8 of a 1026-long bar).
Half-period of the silhouette wave, i.e. one arc (reference: 43.3).
How fast the silhouette wave travels.
Charge fill height as a fraction of the bar interior (reference: 76 of 92.74).
Amplitude of the charge fill's own wave — long and shallow, per the reference.
Half-period of the charge fill's wave. Much longer than the silhouette's.
How fast the charge wave travels.
Inner charge bar thickness, as a fraction of the outer one. Same shape, dodged over it.
How hard the inner charge bar dodges. 1 blows out to white; lower keeps the hue.
Spacing of the background arc texture (reference: 23.83).
Radius of the background arcs (reference: 96.95).
How strongly the arcs show. They only read against the unlit stretch.
End-cap width in logical pixels.
End-cap corner rounding in logical pixels.
How long a ball of light takes to arc from its indicator into the bar.
Pause between one hit landing on a bar and the next setting off.
How long a bar takes to travel to its new value once a hit lands.
How long the OVERLOAD tag and its slow motion last.
How fast the charge gradient drifts along the bar.
How quickly the theme fades out when the battle ends.
Theme level. Lower this if the sound effects are getting buried.
Sound-effect level, mixed against musicVolume.
How fast layers slide to their new slot. Higher = snappier.
Phase offset per slot, so breathing travels outward in waves.
Curve of the radius falloff toward the centre.
Ring thickness as a fraction of the gap to the next slot.
Thickness multiplier for the outermost (active) layer.
Thickness multiplier for every layer behind it.
How long a struck layer flashes white before vanishing.
Beat between the layer vanishing and it regrowing at the back.
How long the regrow beat holds before resolution continues.
Enemy: radius of the outermost ring, in logical canvas pixels.
Enemy: radius step between one layer and the next in. baseR/spacing sets how many fit.
Enemy ring breathing amplitude.
Player: radius of the outermost ring. Huge on purpose — a big circle reads as a nearly flat band.
Player: radius step between layers. Small, so all six sit in a thin arc despite the huge radius.
Player ring breathing amplitude.
Player ring canvas width in logical pixels (wide and short).
Player ring canvas height in logical pixels.
Player: circle centre Y, pushed far below the strip so only the flat top of the arc shows.
Audio bit-crusher quantisation. Low = Atari harsh, high = SNES-clean.
